_note: Model Router version 2025-11-18 routing pool with its deprecated models removed. Use for like-for-like comparison with Model Router. 26 models. `tier` is computed from model_pricing.json (1 = cheapest). Descriptions are what Decision-1 reads to tell the options apart.
tier_status: computed from model_pricing.json version 2026-10-11-global-standard-public-list: ordered by USD input price, then output, cached-input price and name; 1 = cheapest

models.name: FW-GLM-5.3-Flash
models.description: Fast, low-cost GLM model served by Fireworks. Suited to quick drafts, summaries, simple questions and light agent steps with function calling; accepts images. Weaker than flagship models on hard reasoning and complex code. Inference runs on Fireworks infrastructure, outside Azure.

models.name: gpt-5.4-nano
models.description: Smallest, fastest GPT-5.4 model. Good for short answers, classification, extraction, rewriting and simple tool calls at very high volume; supports reasoning, structured outputs and image input. Gives shallow answers on multi-step reasoning, hard code or long documents: choose a larger model for those.

models.name: gpt-5.6-luna
models.description: Smallest GPT-5.6 model: fast and low-cost with a 1M-token context, multilingual support, reasoning, tools, structured outputs, image input and computer use. Good for high-volume work over long inputs; not the best choice for the most difficult reasoning or code.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b
models.description: OpenAI open-weight reasoning model, text only. Good value for maths, logic, code and structured analysis, with function calling and structured outputs. 131K context; less broad knowledge and weaker long-form writing than the GPT-5.x models.

models.name: Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8
models.description: Meta's multilingual, multimodal mixture-of-experts model (12 languages). Good for general chat, writing, translation and image understanding at low cost. No tool calling or structured output; weaker on hard reasoning and complex code than reasoning models.

models.name: grok-4-1-fast-reasoning
models.description: Fast, low-cost xAI reasoning model tuned for agentic tool calling and quick multi-step answers; accepts images. English-focused, 128K context. Choose it for fast tool-using agents and short reasoning, not for long documents or polished long-form writing.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
models.description: DeepSeek open model with visible reasoning; strong at code, maths and agent tasks for its price. English and Chinese, text only, 128K context; tool calling and JSON mode but no JSON-schema outputs.

models.name: gpt-5.4-mini
models.description: Compact GPT-5.4 reasoning model and a good default for everyday work: summaries, extraction, routine code, data questions and tool calls, with structured outputs, image input and computer use. Handles moderate multi-step reasoning; use a frontier model for the hardest problems.

models.name: FW-GLM-5.3
models.description: Flagship GLM model served by Fireworks for complex software engineering, long-horizon agents and reasoning, with tool calling and structured outputs. Text only. Inference runs on Fireworks infrastructure, outside Azure.

models.name: FW-Kimi-K3
models.description: Kimi K3 served by Fireworks: native-vision model for long-horizon coding, agentic tool use and knowledge work over long contexts; strong on code for its price. JSON-schema output is unconfirmed. Inference runs on Fireworks infrastructure, outside Azure.

models.name: claude-haiku-4-5
models.description: Claude Haiku 4.5: fast, low-cost Claude for coding, agents, sub-agent work, extraction and image understanding, with extended thinking. 200K context, Anthropic-hosted (version 1).

models.name: gpt-5.6-terra
models.description: Mid-size GPT-5.6 reasoning model that balances quality and cost: multi-step planning, tool orchestration, coding and analysis over a 1M-token context, with image input and computer use. A strong default for moderately hard tasks.

models.name: gpt-5.2
models.description: GPT-5.2 reasoning model for long-running professional and agentic tasks: analysis, structured output, tool orchestration and code, with image input and a 400K context. Newer GPT-5.4 to 5.6 models are usually stronger at a similar price.

models.name: claude-sonnet-5
models.description: Claude Sonnet 5 for coding, long-running agents, financial analysis and professional writing, reasoning over whole codebases (1M-token context); adaptive thinking, high-resolution image input and computer use. Anthropic-hosted (version 1).

models.name: gpt-5.4
models.description: Frontier GPT-5.4 model for complex professional work: multi-step reasoning, coding, analysis across long documents (1M-token context), tool use and computer use. Use it when a task needs depth that mini models lack.

models.name: gpt-5.5
models.description: OpenAI agentic model for complex multi-step coding, research and data analysis, including synthesis across many documents (1M-token context). Strong tool use, structured outputs and computer use.

models.name: gpt-5.6-sol
models.description: Largest GPT-5.6 reasoning model for complex, compute-intensive work: hard maths, science, code and multi-step analysis over a 1M-token context, with tools, image input and computer use.

models.name: claude-sonnet-4-5
models.description: Claude Sonnet 4.5 for complex agents, long-horizon tasks and high-volume coding, with extended thinking, image input and computer use. 200K context, Anthropic-hosted only.

models.name: grok-4
models.description: xAI reasoning model for hard reasoning and tool use; text only, English. Output is limited to 8,192 tokens, so avoid it for long answers or large code generation.

models.name: grok-4.6
models.description: xAI multimodal model (preview) for coding, engineering, research and agentic workflows; text and image input, tool calling and JSON mode, 200K context. Preview, so behaviour may change.

models.name: claude-opus-4-6
models.description: Claude Opus 4.6 for coding, enterprise agents and computer use, with advanced tool use (tool search, programmatic calling) and image input; 1M-token context. Anthropic-hosted only.

models.name: claude-opus-4-7
models.description: Claude Opus 4.7 for coding, enterprise workflows, long-running agents and multimodal reasoning over high-resolution images; 1M-token context. Anthropic-hosted only.

models.name: claude-opus-4-8
models.description: Claude Opus 4.8 for coding, long-running agents, financial analysis and cybersecurity work, with high-resolution image input and computer use; 1M-token context. Anthropic-hosted (version 1).

models.name: claude-opus-5
models.description: Claude Opus 5: near-Fable capability for long-horizon coding, complex agent orchestration, enterprise workflows and financial analysis; adaptive thinking up to max effort, image input and computer use; 1M-token context. Anthropic-hosted (version 1).

models.name: claude-fable-5-1
models.description: Anthropic's most capable model (preview, Anthropic-hosted) for the most demanding reasoning: long-running agents, coding that needs deeper reasoning, scientific research with self-verification, financial analysis and vision. Extra safety classifiers may refuse dual-use security or biology requests.

models.name: gpt-6-astra
models.description: Frontier GPT-6 reasoning model for the most complex problem-solving, coding, agentic workflows and enterprise knowledge work, with reasoning-effort and verbosity controls, tools, structured outputs, image input and computer use. Use it when answer quality matters most.

cost.instructions: Choose the model that should answer the conversation in the state. Cost mode: choose the cheapest model that can still answer well. Prefer a more expensive model only when a cheaper one would likely give a wrong or incomplete answer.

balanced.instructions: Choose the model that should answer the conversation in the state. Balanced mode: weigh answer quality against cost. Prefer a cheaper model when its answer would be about as good as the best model's answer.

quality.instructions: Choose the model that should answer the conversation in the state. Quality mode: choose the model most likely to give the best answer. Ignore cost.

sources.early_catalog: Model card fields from the project's early catalog (Microsoft Foundry model cards, retrieved 2026-10-10); not published in the docs snapshot.
sources.openai_streaming: Azure OpenAI Chat Completions API supports stream=true for all chat models; the capability tables list it only for some models.
sources.anthropic_adapter: Called through the router's Messages API adapter: tools, parallel tools and streaming are translated, and response_format json_schema becomes output_config.format (Claude structured outputs). response_format json_object has no Messages API equivalent and is not translated.
sources.fireworks_global: Fireworks models deploy as Global Standard and are available from any Foundry region (confirmed by the project owner); inference runs on Fireworks infrastructure.
sources.claude_versions: Foundry numbers Claude versions by hosting: version 1 runs on Anthropic infrastructure, version 2 on Azure. `old` uses the versions Model Router lists (1, or the dated 20250929/20251001 snapshots, treated as version 1); `new` uses the Azure-hosted version 2.
sources.xai_variants: xAI publishes grok-4-1-fast as two deployments, -reasoning and -non-reasoning (retirement schedule); this one is the reasoning variant.
